name: Third camp
summary: The third camp is the socialist position, born in the Second World War, of opposing both the capitalist-imperialist bloc and the Stalinist bloc and organising an independent working-class camp against both. It holds that the Soviet-type states are exploitative class societies, not socialism, and that socialism must come from below through the self-emancipation of workers and the freedom of colonial peoples, with democracy as its condition.
scope: The Shachtman-Draper tradition: the Workers Party's 1940 'Third Camp' statements, Max Shachtman's bureaucratic collectivism, Hal Draper's 'socialism from below', and the Workers' Liberty, New Politics and Solidarity groups that continue it. It excludes Shachtman's later rightward drift into support for the Western bloc, the Iranian Worker-Communist Party's unrelated 'third camp', and orthodox Trotskyists who defend the USSR as a degenerated workers' state. Many modern social-policy answers are inferred from the democratic left stance of today's adherents.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The tradition aims at socialist collective ownership and attacks the profit system and the plutocracy, so it denies markets beat collective decisions.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The statement proposes taking the wealth of the Sixty Families for the masses, which goes well beyond significantly higher taxes.

unions-good.rationale: Independent working-class organisation is the agent of the tradition, and it condemns Stalinism for suppressing it.

property-fundamental.rationale: The tradition wants the plutocracy's property taken and used for the masses, so private property cannot be a near-inviolable right.

worker-ownership.rationale: The goal is a workers' government and workers taking over idle factories, so collective workers' control of enterprises is central.

strong-leader.rationale: Draper's socialism from below opposes rule by an elite or leader standing above the people.

state-harmful.rationale: The state is treated as a danger when it becomes a bureaucratic class instrument, but a workers' state is needed for transition, so adherents stop short of agreeing it is unnecessary.

empower-police-military.rationale: The tradition opposes militarism and both imperialist war camps and distrusts the state's coercive forces.

decide-locally.rationale: Socialism from below favours decision-making spread broadly, but planning and internationalism also require wider coordination, so adherents are split.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The tradition is internationalist and speaks for a world camp of labour, so national culture preservation is no goal.

gradual-change.rationale: The statement calls for a workers' government and says the revolution can be saved only by overthrowing the bureaucracy, a revolutionary rather than gradualist stance.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Johnson notes the tradition rejected world-government illusions and sees great-power blocs as the framework of such organisations.

nation-first.rationale: The Third Camp is a camp of workers and colonial peoples against both imperialist blocs, putting international solidarity over national interest.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Johnson says the tradition backed democratic revolt rather than reliance on NATO, though it supported Kosovars; so support for state intervention is limited.

revolution-justified.rationale: The 1940 statement says the Russian revolution can be saved only by overthrowing the bureaucracy and calls for a workers' government in place of both camps.

experts-over-public.rationale: Draper's socialism from above, rule by an elite, intellectual or technical, is what the tradition rejects in favour of rule from below.

central-planning.rationale: The tradition rejects bureaucratic planning as a class system but supports democratically planned economy; adherents split on whether central planning is superior.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The goal is collective control by workers, not dispersal among small owners.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised bodies setting wages and prices are the opposite of independent working-class organisation that the tradition defends.

one-party-rule.rationale: Johnson reports that Stalinism was seen as the opposite of socialism and that democracy is the condition for socialism.

workers-councils.rationale: The tradition calls for a workers' government and workers' democracy from below; soviet-style councils are its heritage but adherents also value parliamentary democracy.

right-to-secede.rationale: Johnson says self-determination is a democratic demand including the right to secession.

natural-rulers.rationale: The two-souls thesis condemns elitist rule by those deemed fit to administer others.

political-violence-never.rationale: The tradition supports revolution and armed self-defence by workers and oppressed peoples, so political violence is not always wrong.

war-builds-character.rationale: The 1940 statement condemns both imperialist war camps and the war as such.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Democratic socialism makes popular will the source of law; scripture-based law is incompatible.

military-superiority.rationale: Both great-power blocs are condemned as imperialist and the tradition opposes the arms race.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The camp unites workers and colonial peoples of all colours across nations; an ethnic national ideal contradicts it.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The statement pits workers against the employers and plutocracy and speaks in class terms throughout; Marxist heritage.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Socialism aims at a classless society, though the tradition does not discuss equality of outcomes as such.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The statement champions colonial peoples against imperialism; reparations are an extrapolation.

self-interest-moral.rationale: A solidarity-based socialist tradition rejects self-interest as a moral foundation.

restore-past-order.rationale: The tradition looks to a socialist future and is revolutionary, not restorationist.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The tradition is theory-driven and regards pragmatic bloc choices as drift toward the lesser evil, as Johnson describes.

direct-action.rationale: The tradition combines workers' direct action, such as taking idle factories, with independent political organisation and elections, so exclusivity is rejected.

means-match-ends.rationale: Draper's central claim is that socialism from below cannot be achieved by authoritarian means from above, and Johnson shows the tradition saw Stalinism as socialism's opposite.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Marx's long-term ideal, but adherents rarely state it; split.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The statement's goal of world socialism and the Marxist heritage point to need-based distribution as the end goal.

production-for-use.rationale: The statement attacks profit and seeks to use the wealth of the few for the masses.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The 1940 statement treats employers and plutocrats as exploiters of the workers, in Marxist terms.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Draper's tradition reads Marx's phrase as working-class democracy, rejecting dictatorship by party, so a dictatorial power over former rulers is not endorsed.

collective-farming.rationale: Stalin's forced collectivisation is condemned with Stalinism, so collective farming as a general rule is not backed.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The 1940 statement explains the world war as one of imperialist camps, tied to capitalism.

taxation-theft.rationale: The 1940 statement calls for taking the wealth of the Sixty Families for the masses, which is incompatible with calling taxation theft.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Workers' collective class rights and self-determination of peoples are central, though individual liberties matter too.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Democracy is the condition for socialism, so the vote matters more than the ability to leave.

state-as-business.rationale: Treating citizens as customers contradicts class-based, collective democracy.

media-academia-power.rationale: The tradition locates real power in the capitalist class or bureaucracy, not in universities and media.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation through families and trade bodies is a corporatist idea opposed to democratic class politics.

total-state.rationale: Johnson reports that Stalinism, a state directing every area, was seen as a neo-barbaric relapse and the opposite of socialism.

national-rebirth.rationale: The tradition is internationalist and anti-nationalist in the war camps' sense.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The statement condemns imperialist war camps and the tradition calls the USSR's expansion imperialist.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Marxist ideology critique pulls one way and scientific socialism the other; adherents are split.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The statement calls for workers' democracy and workers taking over factories.

economic-freedom.rationale: The liberal claim that economic freedom underpins political freedom conflicts with the aim of ending the profit system; adherents instead stress democratic freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Government by rulers' example is an elitist idea the tradition opposes.

national-self-determination.rationale: Johnson reports self-determination is a democratic demand, including secession and armed defence; the tradition stays internationalist.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: A working-class international outlook rejects dividing workers by citizenship.

class-collaboration.rationale: The 1940 statement urges workers to fight their own employers and government, not collaborate.

dominated-front.rationale: The tradition supports anti-imperialist struggle but rejects aligning with a bloc or reactionary regimes against the West.

workers-nation.rationale: The statement stresses an international camp of workers and colonial peoples.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The statement names slaves of all colours and calls for independence from imperial rule.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Johnson reports the tradition analyses the Stalinist state as the instrument of a bureaucratic class, and Marxist heritage treats states as class instruments.

elite-replacement.rationale: A racialised conspiracy claim is contrary to class analysis.

national-mission.rationale: Both camps' claims to defend democracy are called imperialist; mission to spread a government is rejected.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The statement attacks the governments of both camps as serving the ruling class; not framed as corruption.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The tradition wants an economy collectively controlled, not a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The camp unites workers and colonial peoples of all colours.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The statement's internationalism and anti-colonialism assume equal worth.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The statement calls for world socialism and international revolution rather than national socialism.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Adherents are split on this, as Workers' Liberty backs both peoples' self-determination.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Secular Marxist heritage supports it; not directly addressed.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Johnson reports Stalinism as the opposite of socialism, and the tradition rejects the Stalinist rationale for a stronger state.

population-transfer.rationale: The camp is internationalist; expelling minorities is incompatible.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The tradition endorses revolution and workers' defence, so initiating force is not always wrong.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: A solidarity-based class tradition rejects struggle between peoples as progress's engine.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Rule from below against domination by an elite is compatible; the republican wording is not used.

separated-powers.rationale: The tradition values democratic checks but not specifically constitutional separation; no stated view.

vanguard-party.rationale: The self-emancipation principle of the tradition counters party substitutionism, though some groups keep Leninist organisation.

priority-to-poor.rationale: A labour tradition prioritises the needs of workers and poor; the phrase is not used.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The tradition defends independent working-class organisation against restriction, and condemns suppression of it by Stalinist regimes.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The tradition blames the profit system and the plutocracy, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The 1940 statement calls on workers and colonial peoples of all colours to unite, treating diversity as no obstacle to solidarity.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Rule from below might favour it but adherents emphasise election and recall; no stated view.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The tradition treats democracy as the condition of socialism and condemns Stalinist police states.

party-controls-media.rationale: Johnson reports Stalinist control of society as the opposite of socialism; the tradition demands democratic freedoms.

party-commands-army.rationale: Party control of the armed forces typifies Stalinist bureaucratic rule, which is rejected.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Adherents are split on democratic centralism versus open dissent.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The tradition wants international unity from below but does not endorse the EU as a capitalist union; split.

head-commands-forces.rationale: A presidential military command contradicts democratic accountability.

clerical-rule.rationale: Clerical rule is incompatible with democracy, the condition of socialism.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The statement tells workers to fight their own government and employers during the war rather than support either camp.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The tradition condemns Stalinist control of culture and wants democratic freedom.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The camp is international and rejects ethnic membership.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The statement links colonial independence to world socialism, though not the economy specifically.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Stalinist forced industrialisation under dictatorship is condemned as the opposite of socialism.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The tradition opposes both blocs' arms race; Draper called the West's H-bombs its enemy per Johnson.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Marxist critique denies private property of the means of production; the statement is weaker, so agreement is qualified.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Shachtman called the USSR bureaucratic collectivism, a new class society, rejecting the state capitalist label that Cliff used, while all agree it is not socialism.

collective-defense.rationale: Johnson reports the tradition refused to back NATO or Warsaw as lesser evil.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Prefers abolition of monarchy; ceremonial head not directly addressed.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Johnson reports the right to secession is a democratic demand.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The tradition wants the wealthy taxed more heavily and expropriated.

character-from-environment.rationale: Marxist materialism leans to environment; not directly addressed.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Mixed rule gives the few power, contrary to rule from below.

leader-cult.rationale: The Stalinist leader cult is part of what Johnson says the tradition condemns.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The tradition says a bureaucracy can become the ruling class, but does not accept the Maoist frame; split.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The camp is an internationalist class alliance across borders, so claiming territory because people of one nationality live there contradicts it.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Marxist heritage; Draper stressed class agency too, so qualified.

no-bailouts.rationale: Adherents split between opposing bank bailouts and saving jobs.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Democracy is central but minority protections matter; split.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The camp is internationalist and anti-imperialist.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The tradition stresses self-emancipation of the working class rather than substitution by a small group.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Democracy as the condition of socialism rejects hereditary privilege.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Johnson reports the tradition saw capitalism's decay feeding Stalinist barbarism, doubting stable adaptation.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The 1940 statement opposes imperialism in all forms.

delink-world-market.rationale: Anti-imperialist but internationalist, favouring workers' solidarity over autarky.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The camp is built on working-class unity across countries, so the idea that rich-country workers are not exploited is rejected.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The tradition's call to unite workers and colonial peoples of all colours is opposed to a right to refuse service on any grounds.

elective-rulers.rationale: Johnson reports democracy as the condition of socialism, so rulers are chosen by election, not heredity.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Popular revolt against rulers is endorsed in Johnson's account of East Berlin and Hungary.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Paternalist duty of elites is contrary to self-emancipation.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The statement calls on workers to organise and fight.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A Marxist heritage critique of how class society reproduces itself through culture; the sources opened do not discuss it.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Marxist tradition holds that rulers sustain power through ideas as well as force, though the sources opened do not state it.

native-born-offices.rationale: Reserving offices for the native-born conflicts with the international solidarity of workers and colonial peoples.

party-own-road.rationale: The tradition rejected Moscow's direction of foreign parties and called for independent socialism.

return-lost-territory.rationale: The camp opposes nationalist rivalry between states, so demanding lost territory back contradicts its internationalism.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Democratic equality opposes group-based political leadership.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The tradition condemns Stalinism as totalitarian but rejects equating socialism with fascism; split.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Democracy is universal condition of socialism.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Contrary to democratic control; Stalinist and military rule condemned.

office-by-exam.rationale: Rule by officials chosen by exam is a form of rule from above.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Johnson notes Shachtman's drift to supporting Bay of Pigs and arming Hungarians, which Draper opposed.

democratic-peace.rationale: The tradition sees capitalist democracies as imperialist.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The tradition backs revolution against the bureaucracy yet respects democratic law, so adherents have no settled position.

non-intervention.rationale: Anti-imperialist but supports solidarity with revolts; split.

informal-organisation.rationale: The tradition emphasises class organisation, not small informal groups.

religious-nation.rationale: The camp is of workers of all colours; secular.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The Marxist heritage separates personal belongings from the means of production that are held in common; the sources opened do not state it.

defeat-communism.rationale: The tradition wanted democratic revolt against Stalinism, not Western domination, and Shachtman's drift is a deviation.

religion-illusion.rationale: Marx's view of religion as consolation is part of the heritage, though the sources opened do not address it and adherents oppose state atheism.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Marxist heritage treats capitalism as progressive historically before it becomes a barrier; the sources opened do not state it.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Marxist heritage links equality to transformation of the economy; the sources opened do not address it.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The tradition aims at a society-wide workers' democracy, not small communities.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Criminalising private sexual conduct contradicts the civil liberties that the tradition makes a condition of socialism.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Johnson reports Stalinist suppression is condemned as the opposite of socialism.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The statement names colonies as oppressed peoples and demands their independence.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Draper's socialism from below places decisions broadly with the people.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The camp sits on the socialist left and is defined by class opposition.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist heritage claim about wage labour; the sources opened do not discuss alienation.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Democracy as the condition of socialism puts authority in the people, not in God.

social-market-economy.rationale: The tradition aims past capitalism to collective ownership, so a regulated market economy is at best a reform stage.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Not pacifist; workers' militias are a tradition.

rich-first.rationale: The statement seeks the wealth of the few for the masses, rejecting letting some grow rich first.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The slogan is neither Washington nor Moscow, though Johnson says it rejected neutralism.

property-franchise.rationale: Johnson reports democracy as the condition of socialism, and a property franchise denies workers the vote.

reification.rationale: A Marxist heritage concept; the sources opened do not discuss it.

racial-franchise.rationale: The camp unites workers and colonial peoples of all colours, rejecting a racial vote.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The statement attacks the plutocracy's control.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Boycotts of a minority's shops are prejudice that divides workers, contrary to the camp's unity.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The statement attacks the Sixty Families of the plutocracy.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: State imposition on belief contradicts the democratic freedoms the tradition requires, and Stalinist state ideology is condemned.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Collective, democratic provision is preferred to reliance on private charity for the poor.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The slogan rejects both Washington and Moscow, capitalism and Stalinist bureaucratic collectivism; a socialist third course, though not what adherents call communism.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Johnson reports the tradition treats democracy as the condition of socialism and condemns Stalinist rule by an unaccountable bureaucracy, so a ruler above the law is rejected.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The 1940 statement names India, Indo-China and Morocco among oppressed peoples and demands their independence from imperialism, rejecting tutelage by advanced powers.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The tradition arose in opposition to Soviet domination of its bloc, and Wikipedia describes the USSR as an imperialist power, so troops sent to stop an ally leaving are condemned.

corporate-influence.rationale: The 1940 statement attacks the Sixty Families of the American plutocracy, whose economic power the tradition says shapes government policy and war.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Johnson's account makes democracy the condition of socialism and rejects Stalinist one-man rule; hereditary succession of a leader contradicts both.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: A socialist tradition aiming to end exploitation of labour by owners and by bureaucrats, in Draper's socialism from below.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The tradition is not pacifist and supports workers' defence and anticolonial struggle, though it opposes imperialist war.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: A Marxist class analysis treats politics as a struggle of classes and interests, not of spiritual forces.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Internationalist socialism rejects tying economic life to a national majority, and stands for equal rights of minorities.

independent-unions.rationale: The Third Camp insists on an independent working-class camp against both blocs and rejects Stalinist state-controlled unions.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Draper's socialism from below and Shachtman's bureaucratic collectivism say the Soviet states are not socialism because workers lack power.

person-over-state.rationale: Alan Johnson's account stresses democracy and civil liberties, and socialism from below treats the person as an end rather than a tool of the state.

gm-crops.rationale: Not a Third Camp question; adherents split.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The Third Camp calls for the unity of world labour and rejects dividing workers by race; the 1940 statement addresses all workers.

racial-pride.rationale: Its internationalist working-class politics stress solidarity across races, treating racial pride as divisive though pride in oppressed peoples' struggles is accepted.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The 1940 statement rejects both imperialist war camps and calls on workers to step in and end the war, but it does not call on soldiers to refuse service, and the Trotskyist tradition opposed individual refusal.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Independent workers' organisation is central to self-emancipation, though bargaining is seen as a stepping stone.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The tradition backs colonial independence and self-determination against imperialist domination.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Socialism from below means workers' power replacing the capitalist state rather than inheriting it, though adherents stress democracy.

sacred-nation.rationale: The tradition is internationalist and rejects loyalty to either nation-state camp, treating class as the basic community.

workers-own-party.rationale: The Third Camp calls for an independent camp of world labor against both blocs, and its organisations built their own workers' parties.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Shachtman's tradition broke with Trotsky in 1940 by refusing to defend the Soviet Union, which it called bureaucratic collectivist, and held that the USSR's defeat would be the best result for the working class.

indirect-election.rationale: Adherents' socialism from below favours democratic councils but also direct democracy, and the sources do not settle which.

self-ownership.rationale: Adherents value individual freedom from below but frame rights collectively; the tradition never takes up the self-ownership doctrine.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Its core idea is workers' self-emancipation from below, with democratic workers' bodies and unions, so it rejects a leader ruling over the people and bypassing their organisations.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: The tradition defends civil liberties and resistance from below, but as Marxists its adherents do not generally rely on natural-law claims, so the answer is split.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: The 1940 statement rejects support for either war camp and calls for the camp of world labor, so national loyalty is treated as dividing workers.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: The tradition holds that Soviet-type party states are exploitative bureaucratic-collectivist class societies and that socialism requires democracy from below.

police-more-powers.rationale: The tradition opposes militarism and both imperialist war camps and distrusts the state's coercive forces. (Moved from empower-police-military, 2026-11-11, when that statement became about military spending alone.)

missingStatements.text: State ownership of the economy does not make a society socialist unless the people control it democratically.
missingStatements.rationale: Johnson reports the tradition held that nationalised property alone did not make a society socialist and criticised orthodox Trotskyists' fixation on nationalisation.
missingStatements.declined: This audit answers soviet-state-capitalist as split, so it cannot be merged; the claim is a theory-internal point.

missingStatements.text: Socialism must be won by the working class acting for itself, not introduced for it by a party or state from above.
missingStatements.rationale: Shachtman's formulation that the emancipation of the working class is the task of the working class itself, and Draper's socialism from below, are core.

missingStatements.text: In a conflict between rival great-power blocs, one should support neither bloc, even as the lesser evil.
missingStatements.rationale: The slogan 'Neither Washington nor Moscow' and the refusal of critical support for either bloc define the tradition per Johnson, and the 1940 statement rejects both war camps.

notes: Contested: the USSR is bureaucratic collectivist for Shachtman but state capitalist for Cliff's followers. Shachtman himself later drifted toward backing the West, so some self-described adherents would answer Cold War questions differently.
